meta.description: Validates docked / generated protein-ligand poses using PoseBusters physical-validity tests, strain energy quantification, geometric checks (planarity, vdW overlap, bond/angle distortion), and pose-energy reasonableness. Use when QC-ing docking results, comparing classical vs ML docking outputs, or filtering pose lists before SAR analysis.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID, trial results, or statistics. All numeric claims in the fixed SKILL.md were independently re-verified against a running installation: dock=22/redock=28 columns (my own script, reaudit_dock_vs_redock.py), the strain value 4.162648 kcal/mol (reproduced 3x, deterministic), and the 0.29 Å pass / 0.42-0.45 Å fail planarity bracket (reproduced with a different ring atom and different step series than either the original auditor or the fixer used).

practice_boundaries.detail: Purely computational cheminformatics QC on docked poses; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about a patient.

methodological_ground.detail: Unchanged from the original audit's finding: the Skill correctly avoids overgeneralizing benchmark numbers and frames strain energy as a diagnostic, not a rigorous free energy. The fix pass added new empirical claims (the planarity bracket) with correct hedging ('roughly double', 'reliably passes/fails') rather than asserting a new false-precision cutoff.

code_usability.detail: All 7 inputs' code ran to completion with no syntax errors or missing dependencies. examples/validate_poses.py now has a real, runnable __main__ (previously a no-op) that I independently re-ran 3x, reproducing the fixer's exact strain value each time.

functional_suitability.note: Same broad, well-matched coverage as the original audit. Correctness improved from 10->11: the dock-config claim was independently re-verified as now accurate (5-column gap, not just RMSD). Still docked 1 point: re-audit found a new, unaddressed factual gap -- the `mol` config table row still lists 'stereo' as included, but the installed library's `mol` config has no tetrahedral_chirality/double_bond_stereochemistry columns (verified directly), contradicting the fix's own new caveat sentence three lines above the table.

reliability.note: Unchanged from the original audit. Common Errors table now also covers the filter-vs-reject pitfall (moved in from usage-guide.md), but the PDBQT-to-SDF bond-order conversion pitfall a real Vina-docking user hits before ever calling PoseBusters is still undocumented.

performance_context.note: Unchanged. SKILL.md length and structure are unaffected by the fix; the new fixtures/ files live under examples/, not inline.

agent_usability.note: Improved from 14->15: the Common Errors table now covers all issues the original audit found, and the dock-config table row is precise about which checks require mol_true. Docked 1 point for the new mol-config-row/stereo inconsistency (see functional_suitability), which sits exactly where an agent skimming the config table for a quick answer would be misled.

maintainability.note: Improved from 9->11: examples/validate_poses.py now ships real fixtures (RCSB 3PTB, CC0 receptor + a real Vina-redocked benzamidine pose) and a runnable, assertion-backed __main__ block, independently re-verified here. The redundancy pass also removed usage-guide.md's restatements of SKILL.md content, improving modularity without losing any agent-actionable guidance (verified by diffing old vs. new usage-guide.md).

inputs.label: "I docked a chiral fragment blind (no reference structure) and QC'd it with the Skill's 'dock' config -- does PoseBusters actually catch a chirality-inverted pose that way, or only under redock?" -- (R)-1-phenylethanol vs its (S) enantiomer, a molecule and chemotype used nowhere else in this audit or the fixer's checks.
inputs.note: redock (with mol_true = correct R enantiomer) correctly flags tetrahedral_chirality=False for the inverted S pose. dock and mol configs both lack the tetrahedral_chirality column entirely -- structurally incapable of catching the inversion, exactly as the fix's new caveat warns. But this also surfaced an unfixed defect: SKILL.md's config table still lists 'stereo' as part of what `mol` config includes, which is false (verified: mol config has 12 columns, none of them tetrahedral_chirality or double_bond_stereochemistry) and contradicts the fix's own caveat sentence.

assertions.text: redock config with the correct enantiomer as mol_true flags a stereo-inverted docked pose via tetrahedral_chirality=False
assertions.note: Verified on a molecule/system used nowhere else in this audit.

assertions.text: dock config (no reference) structurally cannot catch the same inversion -- no tetrahedral_chirality column is present at all
assertions.note: Confirmed: dock config returns 12 columns for this ligand-only case (no organic/inorganic-cofactor columns triggered), none of them chirality-related.

assertions.text: The Skill's new caveat ('chirality/stereo checks only run when mol_true is supplied') correctly predicts this behavior for a molecule outside the benzamidine/3PTB system used throughout the rest of the audit
assertions.note: Caveat holds on an independent chemotype, not just the system it was verified against during the fix.

assertions.text: SKILL.md's `mol` config table row ('Intra-ligand only: sanity, bonds, angles, rings, stereo, energy') accurately reflects the installed library's mol-config columns
assertions.note: New finding, not caught by the original audit or the fix pass. mol config returns 12 columns (mol_pred_loaded, sanitization, inchi_convertible, all_atoms_connected, no_radicals, bond_lengths, bond_angles, internal_steric_clash, aromatic_ring_flatness, non-aromatic_ring_non-flatness, double_bond_flatness, internal_energy) -- no tetrahedral_chirality, no double_bond_stereochemistry. The row's 'stereo' claim directly contradicts the caveat added 3 lines above the table in this same fix.

inputs.label: "A colleague's SVD ring-planarity check said a 0.6 A ring pucker was fine but flagged 1.0 A as bad -- does PoseBusters' real check agree, and where does the true cutoff fall?" -- independent series: a different ring atom than either the original auditor's or the fixer's puck files, and different step values.
inputs.note: Two independently constructed series (ring atom index 7 of the ring tuple, vs. the fixer's/original auditor's index 0): a fine series (0.15-0.46 A) never failed, and an extended series (0.6-2.2 A) found the real pass/fail transition between 0.29 A (passes) and 0.42 A (fails) by the Skill's own formula -- closely matching the fixer's claimed ~0.29-0.45 A bracket and clearly refuting the old, removed 0.25 A figure, using different data than the fixer used to derive that claim.

assertions.text: Independently perturbing a different ring atom with a different step series still finds the real bust() pass/fail transition inside the fixer's claimed 0.29-0.45 A bracket, not at 0.25 A
assertions.note: Transition found between 0.2901 A (passes) and 0.4175 A (fails) -- both inside the claimed bracket.

assertions.text: A pose measuring ~0.29 A by the Skill's own formula -- right at the old documented 0.25 A 'implausible' cutoff -- still passes the real PoseBusters check
assertions.note: 0.2901 A: aromatic_ring_flatness=True. Confirms the removed 0.25 A claim would have misclassified this pose as a false positive for 'implausible'.

assertions.text: The formula and bust() results are deterministic across repeated construction of the same perturbation
assertions.note: SVD-based perturbation is a pure deterministic geometric transform; no randomness in this path.

key_strengths: Both P1 findings from the original audit are genuinely fixed and independently reproduced here with different code and, for the planarity claim, a different ring atom and different displacement steps than either the original auditor or the fixer used -- not just re-run, but re-derived.

The bundled fixtures (RCSB 3PTB, CC0 receptor + a real AutoDock-Vina-redocked benzamidine pose) and the now-runnable examples/validate_poses.py __main__ were independently re-executed 3x here (plus once more via the input2 regression script), reproducing the exact strain value 4.162648 kcal/mol every time.

The redundancy pass is accurate and lossless: diffed usage-guide.md before/after against the fix's own claims and confirmed every deleted section was either a true restatement of SKILL.md or (the filter-not-reject tip) was moved rather than dropped.

A genuinely new test on a molecule/chemotype outside the benzamidine/3PTB system used throughout the rest of the audit (a chirality-inversion probe) confirms the fix's new caveat generalizes beyond the specific pose it was verified against.

recommendations.title: `mol` config table row still claims 'stereo' is included, contradicting the fix's own new caveat
recommendations.problem: The fix correctly rewrote the `dock` row and added a caveat stating chirality/double-bond-stereo checks 'only run when mol_true is supplied (config="redock")'. It left the `mol` row untouched: 'Intra-ligand only (sanity, bonds, angles, rings, stereo, energy)'. Verified against installed PoseBusters 0.6.5: `PoseBusters(config='mol').bust()` returns 12 columns, none of them tetrahedral_chirality or double_bond_stereochemistry -- the same reference-dependent checks the fix pass already established require mol_true. An agent skimming the config table (rather than the caveat prose three lines above it) would conclude mol-only conformer QC catches stereo inversions; it does not.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix pass's diff (verified via `git diff` on the staging commit) touched only the `dock` row and the caveat sentence; the `mol` row was not cross-checked against the same verification.
recommendations.fix: Change the `mol` row's parenthetical from '(sanity, bonds, angles, rings, stereo, energy)' to '(sanity, bonds, angles, rings, double-bond geometry, energy)' or explicitly note '-- stereo/chirality excluded, same as dock; requires mol_true'.
